description: A cursor query may carry POSITIONAL bind placeholders (?) supplied at OPEN through OPEN <cursor> USING (v1, v2, ...). Previously the lexer rejected ? outright and OPEN had no USING clause at all. Pinned with two placeholders bounding a range, with a single one, and - as the regression guard - a plain cursor with no placeholders and no USING, which must still open. Converted 1:1 from scripting/CursorPositionalBindTest (now retired); the blocks are written on one line here, which the scripting parser reads identically.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE invoices (id NUMBER, price NUMBER)

DECLARE c1 CURSOR FOR SELECT price FROM invoices WHERE price > ? AND price < ?; BEGIN LET total INTEGER := 0; OPEN c1 USING (15, 45); FOR rec IN c1 DO total := total + rec.price; END FOR; RETURN total; END;
CREATE TABLE invoices (id NUMBER, price NUMBER)
DECLARE c CURSOR FOR SELECT id FROM invoices WHERE price >= ?; BEGIN LET cnt INTEGER := 0; OPEN c USING (40); FOR r IN c DO cnt := cnt + 1; END FOR; RETURN cnt; END;
CREATE TABLE invoices (id NUMBER, price NUMBER)
DECLARE c CURSOR FOR SELECT price FROM invoices; BEGIN LET total INTEGER := 0; OPEN c; FOR r IN c DO total := total + r.price; END FOR; RETURN total; END;
